title: Academic Words
description: Words for essays, lectures and serious reading — the step before advanced test vocabulary.

words.definition: based on ideas rather than real, physical things
examples: Love and freedom are *abstract* ideas.
His explanation was too *abstract* for the children.

words.definition: to publicly support an idea or plan; a person who does this
examples: She *advocates* free education for all.
He is a strong *advocate* of renewable energy.

words.definition: having more than one possible meaning, so it is unclear
examples: The question was *ambiguous*, so students answered differently.
His reply was deliberately *ambiguous*.

words.definition: clear and logical, with parts that fit together well
examples: Your essay needs a more *coherent* structure.
He was too tired to give a *coherent* answer.

words.definition: so interesting or convincing that you pay attention
examples: She made a *compelling* argument for change.
It's a *compelling* story that keeps you reading.

words.definition: including everything or almost everything
examples: The book is a *comprehensive* guide to Korean history.
We need a *comprehensive* plan.
words.note: Not the same as comprehensible (= easy to understand).

words.definition: to limit what someone or something can do
examples: Our research was *constrained* by a small budget.
Don't let fear *constrain* you.

words.definition: causing a lot of disagreement or argument
examples: The new law is very *controversial*.
He made a *controversial* statement on TV.

words.definition: to reach a conclusion from the facts you know
examples: From the footprints, she *deduced* that the thief was tall.
What can we *deduce* from these results?

words.definition: to become smaller or weaker, or to make something do so
examples: The pain *diminished* after a few hours.
Nothing can *diminish* her achievement.

words.definition: to see or show the difference between two or more things
examples: Can you *distinguish* between the twins?
Children learn to *distinguish* right from wrong.
words.note: distinguish A FROM B / distinguish BETWEEN A and B.

words.definition: to explain something in more detail; (adj.) detailed and complicated
examples: Could you *elaborate* on your idea?
She wore an *elaborate* costume.

words.definition: to show that something is especially important
examples: The teacher *emphasized* the importance of reading.
He *emphasized* every word as he spoke.

words.definition: clear and direct, with nothing hidden or only suggested
examples: The instructions were *explicit*.
She gave *explicit* permission to use her photos.

words.definition: possible and practical to do
examples: Is it *feasible* to finish the project by Friday?
We need a *feasible* solution.

words.definition: basic and most important; forming the base of something
examples: Freedom of speech is a *fundamental* right.
There is a *fundamental* problem with this plan.

words.definition: an idea that can be tested to see if it is true
examples: The experiment supported our *hypothesis*.
Scientists proposed a new *hypothesis*.

words.definition: to put a plan or decision into action
examples: The school will *implement* the new rules next month.
It's easy to make plans but hard to *implement* them.

words.definition: suggested but not said directly
examples: There was an *implicit* criticism in her comment.
Trust is *implicit* in any friendship.

words.definition: certain to happen and impossible to avoid
examples: Change is *inevitable*.
It was *inevitable* that they would meet again.

words.definition: to form an opinion from evidence rather than from direct statements
examples: From her smile, I *inferred* that she was happy.
What can you *infer* from the last paragraph?
words.note: A speaker implies; a listener infers. Noun: inference.

words.definition: being a natural and permanent part of something
examples: There are risks *inherent* in any sport.
Curiosity is *inherent* in children.

words.definition: to give a good reason for something
examples: How can you *justify* spending so much money?
The results *justified* the effort.

words.definition: an idea or belief about something
examples: The *notion* that money brings happiness is too simple.
I had no *notion* of what to expect.

words.definition: seeming reasonable and likely to be true
examples: His excuse sounded *plausible*.
There are several *plausible* explanations.

words.definition: common or widespread in a certain place or time
examples: Smartphone addiction is *prevalent* among teenagers.
This disease is more *prevalent* in warm climates.

words.definition: to improve something by making small changes
examples: She *refined* her essay after getting feedback.
We need to *refine* our search terms.

words.definition: strong and unlikely to break or fail
examples: We need a *robust* system that can handle many users.
The economy remains *robust*.

words.definition: coming after something else
examples: The *subsequent* chapters explain the theory in detail.
*Subsequent* tests confirmed the result.

words.definition: to gradually make something weaker or less effective
examples: Constant criticism can *undermine* a child's confidence.
The scandal *undermined* public trust.
